title: Choose the visual world for Finances
question: Calmer, familiar directions, each with one thing that makes it a pleasure to use. Pick one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Forest Card
options.lineage: Apple Wallet and Things: crisp light screens, one rich colour
options.thesis: A bright, quiet app where free-to-spend lives on one deep-green card you want to look at.
options.viewport: Header with Overview / Money / Plan; a full-width deep-green card holding free-to-spend, per day and the pace line; white panels for Needs you, Still to pay and the three groups.
options.risk: Green for money is the familiar choice; it relies on finish (number count-ups, smooth press) to not feel stock.

options.label: Three Colours
options.lineage: Monzo and Revolut budgets: white ground, a colour per kind of money
options.thesis: Needs, wants and savings each own a colour, so the whole month reads as one filling bar.
options.viewport: Free-to-spend in dark ink at the top; one full-width bar of the month's plan split into needs, wants and savings, filling as you spend; colour-dotted rows below.
options.risk: Three strong colours need discipline; used outside the groups they turn noisy.

options.label: Graphite Days
options.lineage: Linear and Vercel: graphite, sharp type, one bright accent
options.thesis: A precise, calm tool where every day of the month is a bar against your daily allowance.
options.viewport: Graphite header with free-to-spend in white; a strip of daily bars since payday against the daily allowance line, today in lime; light list panels below.
options.risk: Can feel technical and cool to the non-technical one of you.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Copilot Money, Monarch and YNAB's look, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Free-to-spend card with pace chart, a review card, upcoming bills, budget bars; bottom tab bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other finance app by design.
